published_by: NESO / EMR Delivery Body -- the Capacity Market Register, the publisher's own record of every auction it has run
what_this_is: THE PUBLISHED AUCTION OUTCOME, NOT A READING OF IT. The GB Capacity Market clearing price for each delivery year, held SEPARATELY for the T-4 (four-years-ahead) and T-1 (one-year-ahead) auctions, in the unit the auctions clear in: GBP per kW per year of DE-RATED capacity -- together with the published DE-RATING FACTOR for every technology class in every auction. Nothing here interprets them. Which auction a given unit holds an agreement in, which technology class it falls in, whether it won an agreement at all, and what an aggregator passes through to a member are all READINGS, and each lane owns its own.

basis.units: GBP per kW per YEAR, applied to DE-RATED capacity under an awarded agreement. NOT per kW of rated or nameplate power, and NOT an energy price. De-rating factors are dimensionless multipliers on connection capacity.
basis.year_key: delivery_year is the calendar year the CM delivery year COMMENCES. The GB delivery year runs 1 October to 30 September, so delivery_year 2022 is DY 2022/23 and runs 2022-10-01 to 2023-09-30. This is NOT the year the auction was held: a T-4 for delivery_year 2023 was held in early 2020, and a T-1 for delivery_year 2023 was held in early 2023.
basis.t4_vs_t1: TWO SEPARATE AUCTIONS FOR THE SAME DELIVERY YEAR, at different prices AND different de-rating factors, and they must not be averaged or conflated. T-4 procures the bulk of capacity four years ahead; T-1 tops up one year ahead against a revised requirement, is much smaller, and is far more volatile because it is bid against a known-tight margin. In DY 2022/23 the T-1 cleared 11.6x the T-3 for the same delivery year.
basis.price_cap: T-1 auctions clear against a price cap. DY 2022/23's T-1 cleared AT the cap (GBP75/kW), so that figure is a censored observation: it records where the cap sat, not where supply and demand crossed. A model that reads it as a market price has read a regulatory ceiling as a market outcome.
basis.derating_key: A DE-RATING FACTOR IS SET PER AUCTION ROUND, NOT PER DELIVERY YEAR, and this is the single most misreadable thing in the file. A T-N auction for delivery year Y and the T-1 for delivery year Y-N+1 are held in the same round against the same Electricity Capacity Report, so they carry the IDENTICAL factor. Concretely T-4[Y] == T-1[Y-3] -- true for every such pair in this register (DSR: T-4 DY2029/30 and T-1 DY2026/27 are both 0.8558) -- and the substituted T-3 for DY2022/23 obeys the same rule at its own N, matching T-1 DY2020/21 at 0.8614. THE OFFSET IS N-1, NOT N: a T-4 held in February of year H delivers from October H+3. The pass that fetched this register first wrote N, checked it against nine pairs, and was refuted -- recorded because an off-by-one inside a warning about an off-by-one is exactly what a reader skims past. Reading a de-rating factor off the delivery year alone, without naming the auction, reproduces the offset that made `company/market/capacity_market.py` a third disagreeing home for the clearing price. Always key on (delivery_year, auction) together, which is how this file is keyed.

why_native_units: The quantity a CM participant actually earns is clearing_price x DE-RATED capacity x (agreement held), and no publication states that product for any particular unit. Carrying the clearing price and the de-rating factor SEPARATELY, each in the publisher's own units, forces every consumer to perform the de-rating and the agreement condition itself, so both are under test in the lane that does them. That is exactly where the defect of 2026-09-07 lived twice: `company/market/flexibility_potential.py` multiplied GBP75/kW by a household's RATED asset power with no de-rating and no agreement, and `company/market/ic_flexibility_revenue.py` multiplied the T-4 price by an I&C site's RATED flex with no de-rating, overstating its CM leg by the whole factor.

provenance_legend.secondary: read from a publication that QUOTES the auction result rather than from the register itself. NO VALUE IN THIS FILE IS SECONDARY ANY LONGER; the level is kept in the legend because the module that reads this file still accepts it, and because the v1 pass's secondary readings are what the primary pass was checked against.
provenance_legend.contested: two sources give different figures for the same auction and the pass did not reconcile them. NO ENTRY IS CONTESTED ANY LONGER -- the two that were (DY 2023/24 T-1 and DY 2025/26 T-4) are settled by the register.
provenance_legend.not_applicable: no auction of this type procured for this delivery year. Distinct from an unknown price, distinct from zero, and distinct from not_yet_held.
provenance_legend.not_yet_held: an auction of this type WILL be procured for this delivery year but had not been held when this file was fetched. Distinct from not_applicable, which asserts there was never such an auction. The v1 pass had no such level and recorded DY 2026/27's T-1 as not_applicable when it had in fact cleared at GBP5.00/kW.

primary_reached: THE PRIMARY REGISTER WAS REACHED ON 2026-09-07 and every figure in this file now comes from it. The v1 pass recorded 'emrdeliverybody.com returned HTTP 403'. source_urls.fetch_note: THESE URLS 302 TO CLOUDFLARE R2 AND curl DOES NOT FOLLOW A REDIRECT WITHOUT -L. Without it you get an 8-line HTML redirect page written over your CSV and an EXIT CODE OF ZERO. The first attempt of this pass did exactly that and `wc -l` read 11 lines where 51,509 were expected. Use `curl -sL`.

derating_factors.what_this_is: The published de-rating factor for every technology class in every Capacity Market auction the publisher has run, as a multiplier on connection capacity. THE CM PAYS ON DE-RATED CAPACITY: revenue is clearing_price x de-rating_factor x capacity, and a consumer that omits the factor overstates by the whole of it.
derating_factors.keyed_by: (delivery_year, auction) TOGETHER. See basis.derating_key -- the factor belongs to the auction round, and delivery year alone does not identify one. The round-identity is T-N[Y] == T-1[Y-N+1].
derating_factors.dsr_is_not_duration_split: DSR carries ONE factor per auction. Only `Storage` is split by duration, into classes from 'Storage (Duration 0.5h)' to 'Storage (Duration 12h)'. The v1 artefact asserted de-rating was 'duration-dependent for DSR and storage'; the publisher's register says that is true of storage alone. A DSR CMU's de-rating does not depend on how long it can sustain the turn-down, at least not through a published duration class.
derating_factors.the_dsr_series_is_falling: The DSR factor was 0.897 at its peak (T-4 for DY 2018/19) and 0.7145 at its trough (T-1 for DY 2023/24, i.e. the round held in early 2023). It is not a constant and a model that pins one year's value will drift.
derating_factors.suspended_auctions_appear_here_with_no_p: The '2022-23 (T-4)' auction has de-rating factors in this register and no clearing price and no volume, because it was suspended after the 2018 standstill. That is the publisher's own record of a suspension and it is why `t4_auction_actually_held` exists on the clearing-price rows.

participation_rules.minimum_cmu_capacity_note: The minimum capacity threshold for a Capacity Market Unit was reduced from 2 MW to 1 MW, reflecting the deployment of smaller distributed resources. A unit below the threshold cannot hold an agreement in its own right and can reach the auction only by being aggregated, as a Component, into a DSR CMU that meets it.
participation_rules.minimum_cmu_capacity_source: Electricity Capacity (Amendment) Regulations 2020 explanatory note (legislation.gov.uk) and CMS 'Capacity Market: consultation on future improvements'
participation_rules.domestic_households_note: A GB domestic household cannot hold a Capacity Market agreement IN ITS OWN RIGHT: the minimum CMU is 1,000 kW and the smallest awarded DSR CMU in the run window sits at exactly 1.0000 MW, so the threshold binds. THAT IS NOW THE WHOLE OF THE THRESHOLD CLAIM. What this note used to say beyond it -- that a household therefore does not reach the Capacity Market -- IS REFUTED BY THE PUBLISHER'S OWN REGISTER: see `dsr_cmu_shape`. Domestic demand turn-down holds awarded DSR agreements from delivery year 2023, 633.5 MW de-rated by DY2025, under eight named operators. The refusal survives on ONE ground and it is no longer arithmetic: NO PUBLICATION STATES WHAT AN AGGREGATOR PASSES THROUGH to a member household. The '~80 households' arithmetic this note carried is WITHDRAWN -- it divided by rated flex where the register publishes contracted flex, and the observed figure is ~858.
participation_rules.derating: THE DE-RATING FACTORS ARE NOW IN THIS ARTEFACT -- see the `derating_factors` block. The v1 note here said none had been fetched and that any consumer applying these prices to a rated power figure was overstating by the whole factor and must say so. That gap is closed for every technology class the publisher lists. What is still NOT here is what an aggregator passes through to a member, which is bilateral and unpublished, and remains the reason the domestic leg refuses.

dsr_cmu_shape.what_this_is: WHAT AN AGGREGATED DSR CMU IS ACTUALLY MADE OF, read off the publisher's own Capacity Market Register: 18,158 CMU rows and 51,509 Component rows, joined on (CMU ID, Delivery Year, Auction Name), filtered to CMU Technology == 'DSR' with Capacity Agreement Awarded == 'Yes'. This block exists because the domestic refusal rested on ONE DIVISION over two published constants and could not be wrong in an interesting way. The register can be, and it was.
dsr_cmu_shape.it_refuted_the_participation_claim: DOMESTIC AGGREGATION INTO AWARDED DSR CMUs IS OBSERVED, INSIDE THE RUN WINDOW, FROM DELIVERY YEAR 2023. The register carries awarded DSR CMUs whose own component descriptions read 'Aggregated components less than 30KW for DSR GTC' and 'domestic demand turn down', built from tens of thousands of components averaging around 1 kW each. By DY2025 there are 43 such awarded CMU-years, 633.5 MW of de-rated capacity and 713,838 components, held by EIGHT named GB operators including Octopus Energy and Ohme. The prior refusal said a household 'cannot' reach the Capacity Market except through an aggregator; the register says the aggregators exist, hold awarded agreements, and are domestic suppliers and EV-charger operators by name.
dsr_cmu_shape.what_survives_the_register: TWO THINGS, and only two. (1) A household still cannot hold a CMU in its own right: the smallest awarded DSR CMU in the whole run window has a connection capacity of exactly 1.0000 MW, so the 1 MW minimum BINDS in practice rather than being a formality. (2) What an aggregator passes through to a member household is still stated by no publication -- the register publishes capacities and component counts, never a payment. That second one is now the ONLY thing holding the domestic refusal up, where before it was one of two, and the other one has gone.
dsr_cmu_shape.the_eighty_households_figure_is_withdraw: THE REFUSAL CONTAINED THE VERY ERROR IT WAS WRITTEN TO END. '~80 households per CMU' is 1,000 kW divided by a 12.4 kW whole-house RATED flex. The register publishes what a domestic component actually contributes to an awarded CMU: a capacity-weighted mean of 1.1655 kW, i.e. ~858 households per 1 MW CMU. The published figure was 10.7x low because it divided by rated capacity where the register publishes contracted capacity -- the rated-vs-delivered error, living inside the sentence that names it. Independently corroborated: NESO's DFS record says 91% of domestic delivery is below 1 kW, a different publisher measuring a different service and agreeing.
dsr_cmu_shape.the_distribution_is_bimodal_and_the_medi: In the run window, 57 of 1,448 awarded DSR CMU-years (3.9%) are domestic-shaped -- but those 57 hold 973,916 of the 988,138 components (98.6%). Nearly every DSR CMU is a handful of industrial sites (median 1 component, p90 20); nearly every DSR COMPONENT is a domestic premise. A statistic over 'the average DSR CMU' answers a question about industrial sites and says nothing about households, and one over 'the average DSR component' says the opposite. Say which you mean. By de-rated CAPACITY the domestic share is 911.8 MW of 14,860.1 MW, 6.1%.
dsr_cmu_shape.what_a_component_is_not: A COMPONENT IS NOT A CERTIFIED HOUSEHOLD. The register publishes a capacity and a count, not an occupancy. The descriptions say 'domestic demand turn down' and 'less than 30KW', and two of the eight operators (Ohme, Pod Point) are EV-charger businesses whose component is plausibly a charger rather than a dwelling. Every figure here is 'components in CMUs that describe themselves as domestic', which is the closest the publisher gets and is not the same claim.
dsr_cmu_shape.method: Domestic-shaped := an awarded DSR CMU-year whose (connection capacity / total component count) is <= 15.4 kW AND which has >= 80 components. 15.4 kW is the largest whole-house flex in `company/market/flexibility_potential.py`, so the filter is this book's own most generous domestic scale; 80 is the prior refusal's own household count, so the filter is stated in the terms of the claim it tests rather than in terms chosen after seeing the answer.
